questions.question: Who was the little girl that visited the home of the Three Bears?
questions.explanation: Goldilocks is the curious girl who tastes the bears' porridge, sits in their chairs, and sleeps in their beds.
questions.funFact: The original story didn't feature a young girl but rather an old woman who was described as 'impudent and foul-mouthed'!

questions.question: What kind of animal is the Very Hungry Caterpillar before he spins a cocoon?
questions.explanation: He is a caterpillar who eats through many different foods before turning into a butterfly.
questions.funFact: Eric Carle's original idea for the book was about a bookworm named Willi, but his editor suggested a caterpillar instead.

questions.question: In the nursery rhyme, who had a great fall from a wall?
questions.explanation: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall, and all the king's horses and men couldn't put him together again.
questions.funFact: The rhyme never actually states that Humpty Dumpty is an egg! That idea came from illustrations in later books.

questions.question: What color is Clifford, the famous giant dog?
questions.explanation: Clifford is known as the 'Big Red Dog' in Norman Bridwell's popular book series.
questions.funFact: The creator originally wanted to name the dog 'Bloodhound', but his wife suggested 'Clifford' after her childhood imaginary friend.

questions.question: Who went up the hill to fetch a pail of water?
questions.explanation: Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water, but Jack fell down and broke his crown.
questions.funFact: Some historians believe the rhyme is actually about King Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette of France.

questions.question: What kind of animal is Curious George?
questions.explanation: Curious George is a sweet but mischievous little monkey brought from Africa by The Man with the Yellow Hat.
questions.funFact: The creators of Curious George escaped Paris on bicycles during World War II, carrying the original manuscript with them.

questions.question: Which animal huffed and puffed and blew houses down?
questions.explanation: The Big Bad Wolf huffed and puffed to blow down the houses of the Three Little Pigs.
questions.funFact: In early versions of the story, the wolf doesn't just blow the houses down; he actually eats the first two pigs!

questions.question: What type of footwear is Cinderella famous for leaving behind at the ball?
questions.explanation: Cinderella leaves behind a delicate glass slipper when she runs away from the ball at midnight.
questions.funFact: Some scholars believe the 'glass' slipper came from a mistranslation of the French word 'vair' (fur) for 'verre' (glass).

questions.question: What did the boy named Jack trade for magic beans?
questions.explanation: Jack trades his family's only cow for some 'magic' beans, which grow into a giant beanstalk.
questions.funFact: The story of Jack and the Beanstalk is believed to have roots in a fairy tale that is over 5,000 years old!

questions.question: What does the Cat in the Hat wear on his head?
options: A red and white striped top hat
questions.explanation: The Cat in the Hat is famous for his tall, red and white striped top hat.
questions.funFact: Dr. Seuss wrote the book using only 236 different words to help young children learn to read.

questions.question: Who loves eating honey and lives in the Hundred Acre Wood?
questions.explanation: Winnie the Pooh is a lovable bear who constantly searches for 'hunny' in the Hundred Acre Wood.
questions.funFact: Winnie the Pooh was named after a real black bear named Winnipeg who lived at the London Zoo.

questions.question: What did Little Red Riding Hood bring to her grandmother?
questions.explanation: She brings a basket of food to her sick grandmother, but meets a wolf along the way.
questions.funFact: In older European versions of the tale, the girl wears a red cape because red was the cheapest dye available for commoners.

questions.question: What kind of clothing did the emperor wear in 'The Emperor's New Clothes'?
questions.explanation: The emperor was tricked into believing his invisible clothes could only be seen by smart people, so he paraded wearing nothing at all.
questions.funFact: Hans Christian Andersen got the idea for this story from a medieval Spanish tale, but he changed the ending to have a child speak the truth.

questions.question: In 'The Ugly Duckling', what beautiful bird does the duckling grow up to be?
questions.explanation: The 'ugly duckling' was actually a baby swan (cygnet) all along, and grows into a beautiful white swan.
questions.funFact: Hans Christian Andersen considered the story of the Ugly Duckling to be his own autobiography.

questions.question: Who chased Peter Rabbit out of his garden?
questions.explanation: Mr. McGregor chases Peter out of the garden after Peter eats too many vegetables.
questions.funFact: Beatrix Potter originally wrote the story of Peter Rabbit in a letter to cheer up the sick child of her former governess.

questions.question: According to the nursery rhyme, what jumped over the moon?
questions.explanation: In 'Hey Diddle Diddle', the cow jumps over the moon while the little dog laughs to see such sport.
questions.funFact: The phrase 'over the moon' originated from this exact nursery rhyme published in the 1760s.

questions.question: What happens to Pinocchio's nose when he tells a lie?
questions.explanation: Pinocchio's wooden nose grows longer every time he tells a lie to the Blue Fairy.
questions.funFact: In the original story by Carlo Collodi, Pinocchio was actually very naughty and had his feet burned off!

questions.question: What magical item makes Snow White fall asleep?
questions.explanation: The Evil Queen disguises herself and tricks Snow White into taking a bite of a poisoned apple.
questions.funFact: The story of Snow White likely originated from a true 16th-century German countess named Margaretha von Waldeck.

questions.question: What is the name of the bear from 'Darkest Peru' who loves marmalade sandwiches?
questions.explanation: Paddington Bear is found at Paddington Station in London and is famous for keeping marmalade sandwiches under his hat.
questions.funFact: Creator Michael Bond bought a lonely teddy bear from a store near Paddington Station on Christmas Eve as a present for his wife, inspiring the character.

questions.question: Who lost her sheep and didn't know where to find them?
questions.explanation: Little Bo Peep lost her sheep, but the rhyme says to leave them alone and they'll come home.
questions.funFact: The phrase 'Bo Peep' originally meant a game of peek-a-boo in the 16th century.
